assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a simple solution-processed semiconductor into a photovoltaic absorber approaching silicon efficiencies within a decade. The physical principle is clear (high absorption, long carrier diffusion lengths, defect tolerance) and the generative potential is large, spanning tandems, LEDs and detectors. Strong fit with my wish for a clear principle plus new capability.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskite as a sensitizer in a liquid cell; Park and Snaith/Grätzel-group work produced the solid-state, efficient devices. Credit is crowded and the three-person split among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok, Grätzel and Kanatzidis is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently reproduced worldwide and commercial tandem development is under way. Long-term stability is still unresolved, but the discovery of the absorber class is mature enough to recognise.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the first sensitized cell or on the solid-state breakthrough
Long-term operational stability and lead toxicity may still temper the case
Exact priority among several groups in 2012 is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis changed biology and medicine through orders-of-magnitude cost reductions, and rests on chemistry (reversible terminators, fluorescent nucleotides, clonal amplification and single-molecule detection). Impact is enormous and undisputed.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry; Mayer's early clonal-array concept is also credited. Rothberg (pyrosequencing and semiconductor sequencing) and Ju (terminator chemistry) add competing claims, so the three-person configuration is a genuine difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Technology is fully mature and ubiquitous; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Which platform inventors merit credit given several technology lineages
Sanger sequencing was already honoured, so the committee may view this as incremental
Fit as chemistry rather than physiology or medicine

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation uses small molecules to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system and so opens previously undruggable targets. The concept (event-driven pharmacology) is original and clearly explainable, and it is generating a wave of clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, with Ciulli providing the structure-guided VHL ligands and rational design. Molecular glue degraders (Handa, Ito and others) form a distinct strand that may need separate recognition, which complicates the citation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical proof of benefit is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat premature, though the mechanism is well confirmed in many labs.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete
Molecular glues versus bifunctional PROTACs may need different credit
Ciulli's relative priority versus other contributors is uncertain

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing gives single-molecule electrical readout of nucleic acids, a physically elegant principle (ionic current blockade) that matured into portable sequencers. It sits well at the interface of physics, chemistry and biology.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the principle; Bayley engineered protein pores and chemical recognition; Akeson showed strand-resolved readout. Credit is clear in the idea but spread across several people.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices and a decade of use confirm the approach, though accuracy and throughput continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson
Whether the sequencing application or the single-molecule principle is the cited discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, giving chemical control over proteins in vivo. It is original, general and generative.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pairs in living cells; Chin extended to eukaryotes, multiple codons and genome recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed pairs and tools, so the three-name selection has some arbitrariness.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used, with growing applications in therapeutics and biophysics.
uncertainties: Trimming a larger group of contributors to three
Broad impact on non-specialists may be harder to explain than for some alternatives

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks by pairing a deaminase with a programmable nickase. It is a clear chemical idea with direct therapeutic consequences and first clinical results.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group developed the cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related cytidine system. Liu is the central figure and may be the only laureate.
assessment.maturity: Recent (2016-2017) but already in clinical trials; CRISPR itself was recognised in 2020, which may make this look like a derivative step.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize
Whether the committee wants Liu alone or with trainees
Long-term safety and off-target data remain limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, relevant to storage, shielding and catalysis. The discovery opened a whole materials class, though many applications are still at laboratory scale.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum published the first Ti3C2 in 2011; the trio is clear and compact, which supports a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by hundreds of groups but with limited industrial deployment so far, which makes the timing arguably early.
uncertainties: Real-world impact is not yet demonstrated at scale
Reproducibility and stability of the surface terminations vary between preparations

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures create arbitrary nanoscale shapes by design, a physically intuitive bottom-up fabrication principle with many applications in sensing, motors and templating. It connects directly to artificial molecular machines and nanodevices.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami is the pivotal step, building on Seeman's earlier DNA nanotechnology, who is not in the credited list and who died in 2021. Winfree, Shih, Yin and Yan extended the field, so allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method, but the practical impact beyond research tools is still developing.
uncertainties: Seeman's foundational role cannot be credited via this list
Application impact is still modest relative to the conceptual novelty
